name: What is secondary damage, and how can a restoration company prevent it?

mainEntity.name: What is secondary damage, and how can a restoration company prevent it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Secondary damage refers to additional harm that occurs after the initial water intrusion, often due to delayed or improper drying. This includes mold growth, wood rot, delamination of flooring, structural weakening, and damage to unaffected areas from high humidity. A professional restoration company prevents secondary damage by implementing rapid and thorough water extraction, utilizing advanced drying equipment, monitoring moisture levels continuously, and treating affected areas with antimicrobial agents. Their systematic approach ensures complete moisture removal before these issues can develop.
acceptedAnswer.description: Secondary damage is additional harm from delayed drying, like mold or rot. Restoration companies prevent it through rapid water extraction, advanced drying, and moisture monitoring.
